context.job_description: Design, build and run the payment APIs and ledger services for a growing fintech. Work with product and on-call.
context.resume_text:
Senior Backend Engineer, PayLane, 2022 - present
Sharded, multi-region PostgreSQL handling 4M transactions a day.
Built gRPC services in Go; cut p99 latency by 40%.
Backend Engineer, Kinetiq, 2020 - 2022
Event-driven order processing with Kafka.

lines: Thanks for joining today. Could you walk me through your current role?
I lead the ledger team at PayLane. We own the services that record every payment, and I spend most of my time on the storage layer and on reviewing designs.
Let's talk about system design. How would you design an idempotent payments API?

Um, so every write, it takes the idempotency key from client. We are storing the key together with response, in same transaction like the ledger entry, so when retry comes it gives back stored response, not writing two times. Keys are expiring after one day.
What happens if the same request arrives twice at the same time?
There is unique index for the key, so second insert is failing and that request is waiting the first one, then it reads the stored response. We are never relying on application locks for this.
You mention sharding PostgreSQL. How did you choose the shard key?
We are sharding by merchant ID, because almost all queries are for one merchant, so reads are staying in one shard and cross-shard joins are, how you say, rare.
How did you deal with hot shards?
Our biggest merchants created hot shards, so we split them into sub-shards with a lookup table. In hindsight I would have planned for that from day one.
Tell me about a production incident you handled.
One migration was locking a big table in peak hours and payments started to time out. I rolled back inside ten minutes, I was posting updates in incident channel and I wrote the review.
We now run big migrations online in small batches with a lock timeout, and the review checklist asks for that explicitly.
What would you like to know about the role?
How does on-call work for this team, and how are incidents reviewed?
